body:
## Feature request

Make the standalone Agents window the single canonical home for Omni Chat.

## Product behavior

- Omni is available only from the Sessions header in the Agents window and remains gated by `chat.omni.enabled`.
- Editor workbenches do not register an Omni shortcut, Command Center item, Chat title action, Command Palette entry, service, or accessibility-help reference.
- There is intentionally no editor handoff or “Open Agents” shortcut for Omni.
- The Agents window routes against its provider-neutral Sessions catalog rather than aggregating renderer-local catalogs from editor windows.

## Architecture direction

- `vs/workbench` owns a narrow routing-provider contract and does not import `vs/sessions`.
- A `vs/sessions` contribution adapts `ISessionsManagementService` and `ISessionsService` into that contract.
- Candidates come from all registered Sessions providers and exclude drafts, archived sessions, automations, and non-interactive chats.
- Existing requests send through `ISessionsManagementService.sendRequest(..., { background: true })`.
- New folder sessions and quick chats use the provider-neutral Sessions creation APIs.
- Delivery **Open** uses `ISessionsService.openSession` in the Agents window.

## Trust and request context

Provider-owned authentication, policy, Workspace Trust, remote-host behavior, and request dispatch remain authoritative behind Sessions APIs. Attachments are passed through the shared Sessions request option type. Supported model, mode, and permission selections are applied to new sessions; unsupported request-option conversions are rejected explicitly instead of silently discarded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Omni contribution and commands load only in the Agents window.
- [ ] The Sessions header is the canonical gated entry point.
- [ ] The router uses the full provider-neutral Sessions catalog.
- [ ] Existing and new requests dispatch through Sessions APIs.
- [ ] Removed sessions/providers and cancellation produce explicit rejection.
- [ ] Delivery **Open** reveals the session in the Agents window.
- [ ] No cross-renderer broker, catalog serialization, authority identity, heartbeat, resync, or remote action RPC remains.

Implementation is in draft PR #330688.

body:

The follow-up shared renderer changes are in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/264. title: Sessions: Reuse SessionsFlatList for automation run history
body:
Closes #329928

This updates the Automations view to use `SessionsFlatList` for session-backed run history instead of maintaining a separate run-row renderer. History keeps its date grouping and automation-specific Stop/Delete actions while reusing the standard session status, unread state, workspace, changes, and pull request presentation.

Runs that have started but whose session is not yet available in the committed session catalog are shown as lightweight `Working...` rows. Those rows persist through the handoff and are replaced by the real shared session row once the session becomes available.

Automation cards are also keyed by automation ID and updated in place. Run and automation updates no longer tear down and rebuild the full card grid, preserving focus and avoiding unnecessary DOM work.

The shared flat-list support was extended only where needed for this embedding, including custom row toolbars, nested scrolling, deferred read state, and focus restoration. Restored sessions are loaded before cancellation so Stop works for runs that have not been opened in the current window.

title: tunnels: address review follow-ups from #330480
body:
Follow-ups from @dmitrivMS's review of #330480, which merged before the comments were addressed.

### Fixed here

- **Needless tunnel restarts.** `_reconcile` guarded its no-op path on `_currentProcess`, but `_schedule` stops that process and `_reconcile` awaits the stop before reaching the guard — so it was always `undefined` and the guard was dead code. Every intent update tore down a healthy tunnel. Now compared in `_schedule` before anything is stopped, with `restart()` keeping an explicit forced path.
- **Lost sharing intent on failure.** `startHosting` left `_request` and the coordinator's sharing intent set when the coordinator rejected or readiness failed, so a later reconcile could bring hosting online after the caller was told it failed. The abandoned readiness wait also lingered for the full five minute start timeout; its store is now owned by the caller and disposed immediately.
- **Swallowed spawn errors.** The child `error` handler called `reject()` with no argument, so a missing or non-executable tunnel binary surfaced as an undefined rejection.
- **Service mode stuck connecting.** Service mode returned right after installing, so nothing advanced `connecting` -> `connected`, and a failed install dropped the in-session fallback. Service mode now falls through to the session tunnel, which attaches to the installed service's singleton and reports its status — the behaviour that predated the CLI refactor.
- **Editor link advertised for a singleton that does not serve it.** `has_editor_link` described the attaching invocation rather than the singleton attached to.
- **Hosted tunnel identified by display name.** Distinct dev tunnels can share a name, so the hosted-tunnel checks could hide, reset, or disconnect an unrelated tunnel. The dev tunnels ID is now carried from the CLI to `sharingInfo` and both call sites share one `isTunnelHosted` helper.

### Not addressed pending a decision

- `--delegate-to-editor` binds to whichever editor most recently updated the shared registry rather than the initiating one, so with multiple windows on one user-data directory another window can become newest between startup and connection. This was a deliberate simplification when the feature was built, and re-plumbing the initiating instance ID reverses that decision, so I did not make the call unilaterally. Happy to do it if you'd like.

### Notes

Every fix has a test that I verified fails without it.

Both new cross-process fields (the singleton's capability, and the tunnel ID) are optional end to end: a client attached to a singleton from an older build falls back to the previous behaviour instead of silently losing a link or failing to match.

One removal worth calling out: `uses no coordinator-owned tunnel process for service mode` asserted exactly the broken service-mode behaviour, which is why that regression went unnoticed — it is deleted rather than adjusted.

title: github: add reusable platform API service
body:
## Summary

Adds a reusable, typed GitHub API service in the platform layer for future client and Agent Host consumers.

- adds `IGitHubService` as the single composition root under `src/vs/platform/github`
- exposes endpoint, credentials, transport, capabilities, query, pull-request resources, and mutations as plain subsystem properties
- supports caller-provided endpoint, token, and fetch providers so runtimes can supply their own environment-specific seams
- adds generation-aware credentials and stable account resolution
- adds no-store REST/GraphQL transport with account-scoped ETag caching, coalescing, priority scheduling, retries, redirects, bounded downloads, and rate-limit coordination
- adds canonical pull-request/repository/issue resources, subscriptions, typed queries, and safe mutations
- adds deterministic loopback-server and fake-scheduler test coverage

- constructs and registers `IGitHubService` in `AgentService`, but no feature consumes it yet
- does not migrate or change existing Agent Host authentication or GitHub behavior
- leaves the existing OctoKit adapter and all legacy GitHub consumers unchanged
- makes no AHP changes
- makes no Sessions changes
- performs no network requests during service construction

This intentionally establishes the shared platform implementation only. Existing authentication and feature consumers can migrate incrementally in follow-up PRs.

- `npm run valid-layers-check`

body:
## Feature request

Surface agent sessions with failing pull-request CI in the Omni Chat window, alongside the existing sessions that need questions answered or tool actions approved.

## Proposed experience

- Include failing-CI sessions in Omni's existing attention panel/carousel below the input.
- Prioritize questions and approvals before CI failures.
- Show the affected session title and failed/pending check counts.
- Provide a prominent **Fix CI** action.
- Run the fix in the affected session in the background without opening or focusing that session.
- Optimistically remove the card after requesting a fix.
- Resurface the session only when a new head SHA has failing checks.

## Clearing behavior

Clear only the affected session, not the entire carousel:

- Remove it immediately when **Fix CI** is activated.
- Remove it while any new request for that session is in progress.
- Keep it hidden for the current head after a successful Fix CI submission.
- If a different request completes without fixing or acknowledging the current failing head, allow the CI card to reappear.
- Leave unrelated questions, approvals, and CI failures in the carousel.

## Eligibility

Match the Agents window behavior:

- The session is not archived or in progress.
- The associated pull request is open and not a draft.
- CI has at least one failing check.
- A fix has not already been requested for the current head SHA.

## Implementation considerations

- Reuse the existing `BlockedSessions` and `BlockedSessionsCIFixModel` behavior rather than duplicating GitHub polling, prompt construction, or background submission.
- Preserve the `workbench`/`sessions` layer boundary through a narrow provider API owned by Omni.
- Preserve carousel selection across reactive updates.
- Do not load a session chat model merely to display its CI status.
- Keep the **Fix CI** control stable while check counts update so keyboard focus is preserved.
- Use localized, accessible status text and existing orange CI action styling.

## Acceptance criteria

- Failing CI sessions appear reactively in Omni with accurate failed/pending counts.
- Questions and approvals remain higher priority.
- **Fix CI** submits once in the background and removes the current occurrence.
- Passing, draft, closed, archived, in-progress, and already-fixed current-head sessions do not appear.
- A subsequent failing head SHA appears as a new occurrence.
- Existing Omni routing, voice activation, pending prompts, focus behavior, and window sizing are unchanged.

title: chat: fix empty Responses tool schemas
body:
## Summary

- Emits an explicit object schema for parameterless tools sent through BYOK Responses endpoints.
- Prevents strict OpenAI-compatible endpoints from rejecting requests that include tools such as `terminal_last_command`.

Fixes #330610

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Parameterless VS Code tools reach Copilot Chat without an input schema. The language model wrapper preserves that absence as `parameters: undefined`, after which the Responses serializer previously emitted `parameters: {}`. Strict OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints reject that shape because the parameter schema does not identify an object root.

OpenAI's official [function-calling guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#function-tool-example) documents a Responses function tool's `parameters` as a JSON Schema with `type: "object"` and `properties`. A parameterless tool therefore uses the same documented shape with an empty `properties` object.

### Implementation

The Responses conversion now substitutes `{ type: "object", properties: {} }` when a function tool has no parameter schema. Supplied schemas continue to pass through unchanged.

Regression coverage exercises the same parameterless tool through both API modes. Responses now emits the flattened object-root schema, while Chat Completions retains its existing nested-tool normalization.

### Behavior and constraints

- Existing non-empty tool schemas are unchanged.
- `strict: false` remains unchanged.
- The empty object schema does not set `additionalProperties: false`, so it preserves the previous permissive argument behavior.
- The fix belongs at the Responses protocol-conversion boundary rather than on `terminal_last_command`, because any parameterless built-in or contributed tool can trigger the same rejection.

### Review context

The issue was reproduced at the final BYOK request-body boundary. The Responses variant deterministically emitted `{}`, while an otherwise equivalent Chat Completions control emitted a valid object-root schema.

</details>

title: Make the chat input seam structural instead of per-surface offsets
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330483

## Problem

A widget docked above the chat input has a square bottom edge; the input has rounded top corners. Sat flush, the corners leave gaps and the two borders read as a seam.

Every surface hid this itself by pulling the next one up with a negative margin. Because which widget is actually adjacent to the input depends on which ones happen to be visible, the offset ended up different everywhere — `-8`, `-6`, `-4`, `0`, `+4`, `+16` px across surfaces — plus five `:has()` presence checks deciding whose corners to square.

Sharing a single offset was tried twice before and reverted both times: once because the shared value slipped past overrides that only set `margin-bottom`, once because a hide/show pair split across two files tied on specificity, so stylesheet load order decided the winner.

## Approach

The offset is not a property of any member — it's a property of the stack. One container now holds every above-input surface **and** the input. Producers report what their slot is showing and nothing else:

```ts
setChatInputStackSlot(slot, ChatInputStackSlot.Docked);
```

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Empty` | Nothing showing. Ignored, so a hidden slot can sit anywhere in the order. |
| `Docked` | Joins the surface below, which continues the run. |
| `Standalone` | Closes its own box (onboarding card, prompt options, the composer), so the run stops. Still joins a run above it. |

The stack derives which surfaces continue a run and squares their top corners through `--chat-input-stack-radius-top`.

**Why a scan and not CSS:** what matters is the *nearest* non-empty slot above, and `~` matches *any* of them — it would reach past a standalone card to a docked notice above it. Splitting that across competing rules ties on specificity, which is exactly what broke the earlier attempts. `Standalone` earns its place from two independent real cases: the voice/dictation cards, and the prompt-options widget that sits visible between a docked tip and the input.

## What this removes

- 11 negative margins across 7 stylesheets
- A 5-selector `:has()` block and a 4-selector adjacency block in `chat.css`
- 4 `!important` adjacency selectors in the Agents window
- 7 marker classes (`has-notification`, `has-goal`, `has-voice-mode-onboarding`, `has-dictation-onboarding`, `showing-chat-tip`, `showing-prompt-options`, `showing-sub-session-tip`) and the `hostClass` option
- The dead `chat-input-widgets-container` / `chat-status-widget` rules, which had zero TypeScript references

Visibility follows from the same slot state via one shared rule, so producers no longer keep it in a second marker class. A new above-input surface needs one call and gets correct seams *and* visibility, with no CSS of its own.

This is a **coupling** reduction rather than a line-count one: production grows by roughly 160 lines, most of it the new primitive (43 lines of TS, 10 of CSS) and its comments.

## Deliberate exceptions

- **Inline chat** keeps its gap and its own input frame — scoped to the input row rather than `~ *`, so joins between other docked widgets are unaffected.
- **Onboarding cards** report `Standalone`, so the input below keeps its own rounding. This is also what stops the seam depending on notice-lane exclusivity.

## Testing

- **10 unit tests** for the stack contract, including the three regression cases review surfaced: a slot appended *after* another has docked, a standalone slot ending the run, and stale state when a docked slot is removed without standing down.
- **Full suite: 30,701 passing, 0 failing.**
- **Screenshots: 1000 of 1010 byte-identical to `main`.** 6 new fixtures (notice→input, notice→todos→input, and the nested sub-session-tip case); 10 changed, each verified:
  - `chatInputNotice` (2) — this fixture previously hardcoded the squared corner on a fake input, so it would have passed even if the mechanism broke. It now derives the corner, which revealed the staged version was *wrong* for the onboarding card: it drew the card's input squared when in production the card stands clear.
  - `NewSessionComments` (2) — the banner's 8px overlap is gone, so it is no longer clipped. Magnified the join to confirm no gap and no doubled border.
  - `voiceModeOnboarding` (6) — 4px taller as a fixture-only artifact; production clearance is 4px before and after.

## Notes for reviewers

- `isChatInputStackSlotShowing` is currently only called from tests. It's the read side of the API, but flagging it since a production export without a production caller invites the question.
- `.new-session-feedback-banners` reports state but has no slot class — deliberate, as it's always present and zero-height when empty.

Reviewed in draft by three models; all blocking findings are fixed, including an insertion-order bug where a notice docked before its composer rendered never propagated — which would have reintroduced the exact seam this fixes.

title: CopilotCLIModels queries github.com instead of configured GitHub Enterprise host, causing repeated 401 Bad credentials
body:
### Summary

When VS Code is configured to authenticate Copilot against a GitHub Enterprise (`*.ghe.com`) host, the `CopilotCLIModels` component repeatedly fails with `401 Unauthorized: Bad credentials`. It appears to query `github.com` for Copilot user info rather than the configured enterprise host.

### Configuration

```json
"github-enterprise.uri": "https://<company>.ghe.com",
"github.copilot.advanced": {
    "authProvider": "github-enterprise"
}
```

### Observed output

The following repeats on every window reload, several times per session:

```
[error] [CopilotCLIModels] Failed to fetch available models: Error: Failed to fetch Copilot user info: 401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"}
```

Notably, in the same log, Copilot authentication against the enterprise host succeeds immediately before and after the failure:

```
[info] ConversationFeature: Waiting for copilot token or BYOK model to activate conversation feature
[error] [CopilotCLIModels] Failed to fetch available models: Error: Failed to fetch Copilot user info: 401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"}
[info] Got Copilot token for <enterprise-user>
[info] copilot token sku: copilot_for_business_seat_quota
[info] AuthenticationService: firing onDidAuthenticationChange from handleAuthChangeEvent identity change. Has token: true
[error] [CopilotCLIModels] Failed to fetch available models: Error: Failed to fetch Copilot user info: 401 Unauthorized: {"message":"Bad credentials"}
```

So the enterprise token is valid and a business Copilot seat is present, but the CLI models lookup still fails.

### Expected behavior

`CopilotCLIModels` should honor `github.copilot.advanced.authProvider` and `github-enterprise.uri`, and query the configured enterprise host for Copilot user info.

If Copilot CLI integration does not support GitHub Enterprise auth, the feature should be disabled silently for those users rather than logging a recurring error that looks like a broken installation.

### Actual behavior

The component appears to query `github.com` using an enterprise-issued token. Since the user account exists only on the enterprise host and not on `github.com`, the request is rejected with `Bad credentials`.

Chat itself and model selection work correctly. Only the Copilot CLI model list fails, so the practical impact is misleading error noise plus an unavailable CLI model list.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure VS Code with `github-enterprise.uri` pointing at a `*.ghe.com` instance.
2. Set `github.copilot.advanced.authProvider` to `github-enterprise`.
3. Sign in with an enterprise account that holds a Copilot business seat and does not exist on `github.com`.
4. Reload the window and open the GitHub Copilot Chat output channel.

### Additional notes

An image upload in the same session also failed with a 401, which may share the same root cause:

```
[warning] Image upload failed, using base64 fallback: Error: Error uploading image: Error: Image upload failed: 401
```

Troubleshooting note for others hitting this: signing in to `github.com` via GitHub CLI does not help, because the enterprise account cannot exist on `github.com`.

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.133.0
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.61.0
- OS: Windows
- Auth provider: GitHub Enterprise (`*.ghe.com`)
- Copilot SKU: `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`

title: build: Bound transpile file operations

title: mcp: Avoid unchanged server notifications
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #330637

## Problem

The Agents window subscribes to `IMcpService.servers` so its customization diagnostics can include the currently registered MCP servers. `McpService.updateCollectedServers()` is scheduled after MCP collection changes with a 500 ms delay.

Before this change, every collection refresh published a newly allocated `_servers` array, even when `updateCollectedServers()` had matched and reused every existing `IMcpServerRec`. `observableValue` uses reference equality, so downstream observers interpreted that new array as a real server-topology change.

In the Agents window this retriggered `CustomizationsDebugLogContribution`'s full snapshot. One snapshot performs:

- four customization-type passes;
- local, user, and extension storage listings twice per type (24 listings total);
- source-folder discovery;
- one log call per discovered customization and MCP server.

A captured unchanged-state storm repeated roughly every 500 ms. During one 20-second interval, the customization log produced about 39.8 KB/s and 320 lines/s while the Agents renderer averaged 79.2% CPU, peaked at 146.1%, and averaged approximately 3.0 GiB RSS. The storm continued with the side panel hidden, separating it from rendering/compositor work. Native samples showed the expected V8/IPC serialization and allocation/GC pressure from repeatedly sending hundreds of renderer log records to the main-process logger.

## Real-world trigger

No user action was required in the captured run. During a 10-second live storm, 20 complete snapshots were emitted while all five MCP configuration files found across the observed workspace roots retained identical size, modification time, and inode. The user was not repeatedly saving or rewriting MCP configuration.

The existing logs do not identify which background discovery or extension-provider collection produced the equivalent refreshes. Republishing an equivalent collection array is therefore the deterministic developer reproduction of the affected service boundary, not the expected user workflow.

## Root cause

`updateCollectedServers()` already preserves server instances:

1. It matches each current server by collection and definition identity.
2. Matching records are pushed directly into `nextServers`.
3. Only genuinely new definitions allocate a new `McpServer` record.
4. Removed definitions dispose their old server record.

The observable assignment did not use that identity stability; it unconditionally stored `nextServers`.

## Change

Compare the current and next ordered server-record arrays before updating `_servers`. When every record identity and position is unchanged, retain the existing observable value and do not notify observers.

This keeps the existing semantics:

- server additions and removals still publish;
- existing `McpServer` instances remain reused;
- the established ordering remains unchanged;
- definition-specific observables continue to carry updates within an existing server.

The fix is intentionally at the `IMcpService.servers` publication boundary rather than in the diagnostic logger. That prevents every downstream consumer from doing work for a false topology change, while a logger-only dedupe would still expose an unstable service observable.

## Test coverage

Added `mcpService.test.ts` with a focused observable contract test:

1. Build the service with one MCP server and observe `servers`.
2. Republish an equivalent collection array and refresh the service; the observer must not rerun.
3. Remove the collection and refresh; the observer must receive the real topology change.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/mcpService.test.ts --grep 'does not notify servers observers'`
- targeted ESLint for the changed source and test
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `git diff --check`

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A — this occurs in the core Agents window and MCP services
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0-insider, commit `72f433c37ae15b2f1fb8e292a908964ad1673fbc`
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.1 (Apple silicon)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window customization discovery / MCP server discovery
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): N/A
- Logs: `customizationsDebug.log` repeatedly emitted an unchanged full customization snapshot at roughly 0.5-second intervals. Sanitized measurement: ~39.8 KB/s and ~320 lines/s during a hot interval. No prompt or session content is included here.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open the Agents window in a workspace with MCP configuration and a non-trivial customization inventory.
2. Leave the window idle. In the captured setup, a background MCP discovery/provider path republished equivalent definitions at the 500 ms cadence without user action.
3. Observe `customizationsDebug.log` and the Agents renderer process.
4. The same complete customization inventory is rediscovered and logged after each 500 ms MCP collection update, even though the effective server topology did not change.
5. Deterministic developer reproduction: republish an equivalent collection array, or invoke `updateCollectedServers()` twice with unchanged registry state.

## Real-world trigger evidence

During a 10-second live storm, 20 full snapshots were emitted while all five MCP configuration files found across the observed workspace roots retained identical size, modification time, and inode. The user was not repeatedly saving or rewriting MCP configuration. Existing logs do not identify which background collection provider produced the equivalent refreshes; the deterministic republish in step 5 exercises the same service boundary.

## Expected

`IMcpService.servers` should notify observers only when the ordered set of effective `IMcpServer` objects changes. Equivalent collection republishes should not retrigger downstream customization discovery.

## Actual

`McpService.updateCollectedServers()` reuses the existing `IMcpServer` records, but always stores a newly allocated array in `_servers`. Because `observableValue` compares by reference, every update notifies observers. The Agents window's `CustomizationsDebugLogContribution` reacts by performing a full snapshot:

- four customization types;
- local, user, and extension storage listings twice per type (24 listings total);
- source-folder discovery;
- one log line for every discovered customization and MCP server.

A captured hot 20-second interval reproduced the issue with the side panel hidden:

- customization log: ~39.8 KB/s, ~320 lines/s;
- renderer CPU: 79.2% average, 146.1% maximum;
- renderer RSS: ~3.0 GiB average.

During a quiet hidden-side-panel interval, renderer CPU averaged 13.7% and RSS approximately 1.0 GiB. This also explains native samples dominated by V8/IPC serialization and allocation/GC activity: the renderer sends hundreds of log records to the main-process logger for every unchanged snapshot.

## Root Cause

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpService.ts`
  - `_servers` is a reference-equality observable.
  - `updateCollectedServers()` constructs `nextServers` and calls `_servers.set(nextServers, ...)` unconditionally.
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/customizationsDebugLog.contribution.ts`
  - an autorun reads `IMcpService.servers` and starts a full asynchronous snapshot on every notification.
  - single-flight coalescing prevents overlapping snapshots but immediately reruns when marked dirty; it does not suppress equivalent state.

The 500 ms cadence comes from the MCP collection update scheduler. Dropped FSEvents messages are not the direct trigger: the Parcel watcher handles that recognized error by logging it without emitting a file-change or watcher-error event.

## Suggested Fix / Acceptance Criteria

Preserve the current `_servers` observable value when `nextServers` contains the same records in the same order.

- Equivalent collection republishes do not notify `servers` observers.
- Adding or removing a server still notifies observers.
- Existing server instances remain reused as before.
- A focused unit test covers both the equivalent-republish and real-topology-change cases.

title: sessions: fix: avoid disposable context menu actions
body:
## Problem

Opening context menus in the Agents sessions list created short-lived `Action` instances for group operations and extension-contributed commands. `Action` extends `Disposable`, but these instances had no owner, so disposable leak tracking reported them after the menu closed.

The affected paths included:

- Create Group from session rows and non-session list entries
- Add/Move to Group submenu entries
- Remove from Group
- Rename Group and Delete Group
- wrappers around extension-contributed menu commands

## Fix

The transient immutable actions now use `toAction`, which returns a plain non-disposable `IAction`. This matches their lifecycle: their labels, state, and handlers are fixed when the context menu is constructed, and they do not need `Action` change events or disposal.

Extension-command wrappers preserve the original action's ID, label, class, enabled state, tooltip, and checked state while continuing to invoke the command with the marshalled agent-session context expected by extensions.

The dynamically created contributed `IMenu` has a real lifecycle and remains explicitly owned by a menu-scoped `DisposableStore`. It is disposed immediately when there are no actions or from the context menu's `onHide` callback otherwise. Blank-space and group-header menus no longer create disposable stores because all of their transient actions are non-disposable.

The sessions-list documentation now distinguishes these two lifecycles.

## Regression coverage

A rendered-list context-menu suite dispatches real context-menu events for:

- empty list space
- ungrouped session rows
- grouped session rows
- extension-command wrappers
- Add/Move/Remove group variants
- group headers

The tests flatten submenu entries and verify that every transient action is non-disposable. They also verify that the contributed `IMenu` is disposed when the session-row menu closes.

The existing rendered-list test harness was extracted from the rename suite so both rename and context-menu tests share the same service setup and disposal tracking.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run build-fast`
- focused sessions context-menu and rename tests: 11 passing
- ESLint on the changed TypeScript files
- layer validation
- `git diff --check`

title: sessions: fix: show workspace badges in custom groups
body:
## Summary

Custom-group headers identify the group, not the workspace. Sessions rendered under those headers now reuse the existing inline workspace badge that already appears in date, Pinned, and Done sections.

This keeps workspace identity consistent instead of introducing a separate hover-only or trailing label.

## Implementation

- Add `getRenderedSessionGroup` as the shared source of truth for whether a session actually renders under a custom group.
  - Pinned and archived sections retain precedence.
  - Stale membership that does not resolve to a real group is ignored.
- Derive `isRenderedInCustomGroup` from that placement decision and extend the existing workspace-badge condition with it.
- Reuse the same placement predicate when extracting custom-group members during list updates so row placement and presentation cannot drift.
- Share `getWorkspaceBadgeLabel` between rendering and accessibility, including `owner/repository` labels for GitHub remote workspaces.

## Accessibility

The row's accessible name now includes the workspace whenever the standard badge is visible:

- date grouping
- custom groups
- Pinned
- Done/Archived

Ordinary workspace-section rows do not repeat the workspace already conveyed by their header. `InProgress` and `NeedsInput` rows continue to omit workspace from both the visible row and accessible name because live status hides the details row.

## Behavior notes

- The badge remains inline after the workspace-kind icon and before diff statistics.
- It participates in the existing `·` separator logic; fixtures showed no leading, trailing, or doubled separators.
- Long workspace labels truncate using the existing badge styling.
- In phone layout, the reserved toolbar width can reduce a badge to a short fragment such as `vsc…`; this PR does not introduce a phone-specific presentation.

## Tests and fixtures

- Added real-DOM coverage for custom groups, ordinary workspace sections, date grouping, pin/archive precedence, quick chats, live statuses, and accessible names.
- Extracted a shared sessions-list test harness and reused it in the rename tests.

title: Agents sessions context menus leak transient Action instances

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

body:
## Description

Opening a context menu in the Agents Window sessions list can produce `[LEAKED DISPOSABLE]` warnings for transient `Action` instances.

The first observed warning points to `SessionsList.getCreateGroupAction`, but the same context-menu code path creates several other `Action` instances with no owner.

## Reproduction steps

1. Run a Code OSS development build with disposable leak tracking enabled.
2. Open the Agents Window.
3. Open a sessions-list context menu, such as by right-clicking a session row, group header, or empty list area.
4. Dismiss the menu and allow or force garbage collection.

## Expected behavior

All context-menu actions are either non-disposable values or are disposed when the menu closes.

## Actual behavior

The disposable tracker reports an `Action` that was garbage-collected without being disposed:

```text
[LEAKED DISPOSABLE] Error: CREATED via:
    at GCBasedDisposableTracker.trackDisposable (...)
    at trackDisposable (...)
    at new Disposable (...)
    at new Action (...)
    at SessionsList.getCreateGroupAction (.../sessionsList.js:2250:12)
    at SessionsList.getGroupSessionActions (.../sessionsList.js:2229:23)
    at Object.getActions (.../sessionsList.js:2211:35)
    at ContextMenuHandler.showContextMenu (...)
    at ContextMenuService.showContextMenu (...)
    at SessionsList.onContextMenu (...)
```

## Root cause

**Confirmed:** `Action` extends `Disposable`, while `SessionsList` creates short-lived actions inside context-menu delegates without registering or disposing them.

Affected code is in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts`, including:

- `getCreateGroupAction`
- Add/Move to Group submenu actions
- Remove from Group
- Rename Group
- Delete Group
- Extension-command wrapper actions created in `onContextMenu`

The issue is present at commit `cbec6fc64b5adf3dcba6abb102f0a05772f2e878`.

## Possible implementation direction

These actions do not need mutable state or change events. Replace the transient `new Action(...)` instances with the lighter-weight, non-disposable `toAction(...)` helper. Alternatively, explicitly own all created actions in a menu-scoped `DisposableStore` and dispose it from `onHide`.

Add coverage that opens and closes each sessions-list context-menu variant under disposable leak tracking.

title: Support case-insensitive comparison in the diff editor (diffEditor.ignoreCase)

labels.name: *duplicate
labels.description: Issue identified as a duplicate of another issue(s)

body:
### Feature request

Add a `diffEditor.ignoreCase` setting so the diff editor can treat text that
differs only in letter case as unchanged — analogous to the existing
`diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace`.

### Motivation

I work on data-warehouse migration projects where I regularly diff two
revisions of the same SQL script set. SQL keywords are case-insensitive, and
different developers and formatting tools emit them differently (`SELECT` vs
`select`, `FROM` vs `from`). The result is that a file with **zero semantic
changes** renders as fully rewritten, and the handful of real changes are
buried under hundreds of false positives.

This is not SQL-specific. The same problem appears in any case-insensitive
language or format:

- SQL / PL-SQL / T-SQL
- Visual Basic / VB.NET, Pascal / Delphi, Fortran, Ada
- HTML tag and attribute names, CSS property names, DNS names, Windows paths
- Legacy INI / config files

In all of these, a case-only difference is **semantically no difference at
all** — the same category of noise that `ignoreTrimWhitespace` already exists
to suppress.

### Current state

`diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace` is currently the only tolerant-comparison
option available. Neither `diffAlgorithm: legacy` nor `advanced` offers case
folding.

This also cannot be solved by an extension. Folder-comparison extensions
(L13 Diff, Compare Folders, etc.) only decide *which* files get paired up —
the comparison itself is performed by the built-in diff editor. So every
extension in the ecosystem inherits this limitation.

### Proposal

```jsonc
"diffEditor.ignoreCase": false   // default preserves current behavior
Ideally surfaced the same way ignoreTrimWhitespace is — a setting plus a
toggle in the diff editor's gutter / context menu — so it can be flipped for
a single comparison without editing settings.json.

ignoreTrimWhitespace appears to work by normalizing lines before they reach
the diff algorithm, rather than by modifying the algorithm itself. If that is
accurate, case folding could reuse the same normalization hook and keep the
change well contained.

Prior art
Case-insensitive diff is standard in comparable tools:

GNU diff -i / --ignore-case
Beyond Compare, WinMerge, Araxis Merge, Meld, KDiff3
IntelliJ IDEA's diff viewer
Current workaround
Copy both trees to a temp directory, lower-case every file with tr, then
diff the copies. This does surface the real changes, but the diff displays
mangled content, so every hit has to be manually re-located in the original
file. Running diff -riqw from the shell tells me which files changed but
gives up the editor UI entirely.

- vscode.dev asks me if i want to switch to the new branch, which i confirm
- Problem: vscode.dev tries to load the new branch briefly (you can see it in the url) but immediately bounces back to main (url changes back to main)

- if i click the source button again in vscode.dev then i can see the branch listed in the top window. i can also click it, but same behaviour as described above repeats

b) vscode.dev send unauthenticated request to api.github.com -> 404, cause rate limit not exceeded at the time -> switch to new branch works

title: Fix: validate native dialog responses to prevent silent auto-close
body:
## Description

Fixes #329901 (also reported as duplicate #330592: "All dialogs closed automatically").

On Windows, third-party software that inspects native file/message dialogs (for example security tooling) can send an overlapping `CDM_GETFOLDERPATH` / `TDM_CLICK_BUTTON` window message that makes Electron report a `response` outside the range of buttons that were actually shown (observed value: `420`, see electron/electron#52747).

Traced the propagation of that bad response through this codebase:

1. `DialogMainService#showMessageBox` indexed into `buttonIndeces` with the raw Electron response. An out-of-range value silently produced `undefined` there.
2. That `undefined` crossed the IPC boundary and reached `AbstractDialogHandler#getPromptResult`, where `promptButtons[buttonIndex]?.run(...)` short-circuited on the optional chain — **no button's action ran at all**.

The dialog just closes with nothing having happened, which is indistinguishable from the dialog "closing itself" — matching the symptom reported in both issues, including the Source Control commit-confirmation flow.

## Changes

- `dialogMainUtils.ts`: adds `resolveMessageBoxResponse`, which maps an out-of-range response to the dialog's own cancel button (or its last button, the same least-destructive default `massageMessageBoxOptions` already uses) instead of leaving it `undefined`.
- `dialogMainService.ts`: uses the new helper in `showMessageBox` and logs an error when a fallback was needed, so this is diagnosable from user logs.
- `dialogs.ts` (`AbstractDialogHandler#getPromptResult`): adds an independent defensive fallback to the prompt's cancel button for an out-of-range index, since this method is shared by the native, custom, and mobile-aware dialog handlers.

## Note for reviewers

I'm aware `deepak1556`/`sbatten` already have draft PR #330128 in flight for this same issue with a broader approach (response validation + logging + fallback to custom dialogs). Opening this in case a narrower, independently-derived fix is useful in the meantime — happy to close this in favor of #330128 if/when it lands, or to adjust based on feedback.

## Testing

- Added unit tests in `dialogMainUtils.test.ts` covering in-range passthrough, out-of-range response with a valid/invalid/disabled `cancelId`, and the degenerate single-button case.
- Added `dialogs.test.ts` covering `getPromptResult`: valid index runs the right button, out-of-range index falls back to the cancel button, out-of-range index with no cancel button preserves today's no-op behavior.
- `./test/unit/electron` run for `src/vs/platform/dialogs/**`: 20/20 passing, no regressions.
- `eslint` on changed files: clean.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the full `src` tree: clean.

Type: Bug Native modal dialogs dismiss themselves immediately on Windows (1.133.0, Electron 42.8.0) --- Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled (`code --disable-extensions`)? **Yes** - VS Code Version: 1.133.0 - Commit: a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960 - Date: 2026-08-11T22:14:08Z - Electron: 42.8.0 - Architecture: x64 - OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (10.0.26200) - Display: 1920x1080 @ 59Hz, single monitor, Intel UHD Graphics ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a folder that is a Git repository. 2. Modify a tracked file so it appears as a change in Source Control. 3. In the Source Control view, click **Discard Changes** on that file. ## Expected The "Are you sure you want to discard changes in ?" confirmation dialog opens and stays open until a button is clicked. ## Actual The dialog appears for a fraction of a second and then closes itself. No button is ever clicked and no action is taken. It is impossible to confirm the operation. This is **not** specific to Git. Other native confirmation dialogs (file delete confirmation, overwrite prompts) behave the same way. Any native modal dialog self-dismisses. ## Key diagnostic — one machine, one build, single-variable comparison All three rows below are the same machine, same VS Code 1.133.0 install, same `argv.json`, run within minutes of each other: | # | dialog backend | user-data-dir | Result | |---|---|---|---| | A | native (default) | normal profile | **Dialog self-dismisses** | | B | native (default) | fresh `--user-data-dir` | Works correctly | | C | `window.dialogStyle: custom` | normal profile | Works correctly | A vs B differ only in user-data-dir contents. A vs C differ only in the dialog backend. So the failure requires the **native** dialog path AND something in an existing user-data-dir. Either variable alone is enough to avoid it. ## Workaround ```json "window.dialogStyle": "custom" ``` Effective immediately, no restart required. ## Ruled out (with evidence, not assumption) - **GPU / hardware acceleration.** `~/.vscode/argv.json` has `"disable-hardware-acceleration": true`. Per `out/main.js`, `argv.json` resolves from `os.homedir()`, not the user-data-dir, so it was equally active in the failing run (A) and the working run (B). Passing `--disable-gpu` changed nothing, as expected. - **Extensions.** Reproduces with extensions disabled. Note also that `--user-data-dir` does not change the extensions directory, so run B loaded the identical extension set and still worked. - **`keybindings.json`.** No such file exists in this profile; nothing is binding Escape or Enter. - **`settings.json`.** Contains no window-, dialog-, or modal-related keys. `window.dialogStyle` was unset, so the default `"native"` was in effect. - **Installation integrity.** Exactly one runtime directory present (`a5b5009513`), no stale runtime dirs, install directory shared by runs A and B. ## Profile characteristics (in case the triggering state is size- or age-related) This user-data-dir has been in continuous use since 2022: - `User\workspaceStorage`: 141 entries - `WebStorage`: 803 MB across per-partition directories dating back to 2024 (two directories alone account for 680 MB) - `Cache`: 197 MB - `globalStorage\state.vscdb`: 293 items, including keys from long-removed features (e.g. `window.experimental.useSandbox`, a string that no longer appears anywhere in the 1.133.0 bundle) I have not isolated which component triggers it. I can bisect the profile on request if that would help. ## Additional observations Under the failing profile the main process is under sustained load. If native modal creation is sensitive to main-process responsiveness or to window focus state at the moment the dialog is shown, that may be what links the two variables above. Extension host stalls, from `logs\\window1\renderer.log`, across two separate sessions today: ``` 2026-08-13 11:04:01.444 [info] Extension host (LocalProcess pid: 26032) is unresponsive. 2026-08-13 11:04:03.863 [info] UNRESPONSIVE extension host: starting to profile NOW 2026-08-13 11:04:04.821 [info] UNRESPONSIVE extension host: received responsive event and cancelling profiling session 2026-08-13 11:13:48.696 [info] Extension host (LocalProcess pid: 25296) is unresponsive. ``` Git command latency, from `logs\\window1\exthost\vscode.git\Git.log` (73 timed commands in one session): ``` median 300 ms over 1000 ms 14 of 73 ``` Representative run of back-to-back invocations of the same command: ``` 2026-08-13 11:10:03.754 [info] > git rev-parse --show-toplevel [586ms] 2026-08-13 11:10:13.885 [info] > git rev-parse --show-toplevel [482ms] 2026-08-13 11:10:14.105 [info] > git rev-parse --show-toplevel [214ms] 2026-08-13 11:10:14.412 [info] > git rev-parse --show-toplevel [300ms] 2026-08-13 11:10:14.722 [info] > git rev-parse --show-toplevel [305ms] 2026-08-13 11:10:15.000 [info] > git rev-parse --show-toplevel [272ms] ``` A `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` on a warm repository would normally complete in well under 50 ms. ## Affected vs unaffected machines Same 1.133.0 build across the team; some machines affected, some not. | Machine | OS build | Monitors / scaling | workspaceStorage entries | WebStorage | Profile created | Affected | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 (reporter) | 10.0.26200 | 1 x 1920x1080 @ 100% | 141 | 803 MB | 2022 | **Yes** | ## Available on request - Screen recording of the dialog opening and self-dismissing - Full `renderer.log`, `main.log` and `vscode.git\Git.log` from a failing session - Bisect of the user-data-dir to isolate which component triggers it - `--verbose` startup log, or a trace-level log via `--log trace` ## Possibly related - #321312 — "Freeze when opening any dialog V1.123+", labeled `electron-42-update`. Different symptom (freeze rather than self-dismiss) and labeled `linux`, but the same workaround applies and it also begins after the Electron 42 update. Closed as not planned. - electron/electron#51988 — upstream issue referenced from the above. <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (User Setup, x64)
- Commit: `a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`
- Electron: 42.8.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise, 10.0.26200, x64
- `network.meteredConnection`: `auto` (the default)
- Latest Insiders: Not tested because it is not installed. The current `main` branch still contains the same detection logic described below.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In Windows Settings, mark the active network as a metered connection.
2. Confirm that the Windows Runtime API reports a costed connection. PowerShell 7 cannot load this WinRT type directly, so invoke Windows PowerShell 5.1 explicitly (the following command can be pasted into a PowerShell 7 terminal):

   ```powershell
   powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command '$null = [Windows.Networking.Connectivity.NetworkInformation, Windows.Networking.Connectivity, ContentType = WindowsRuntime]; $profile = [Windows.Networking.Connectivity.NetworkInformation]::GetInternetConnectionProfile(); $profile.GetConnectionCost() | Format-List NetworkCostType, Roaming, OverDataLimit, BackgroundDataUsageRestricted'
   ```

   On my system, `NetworkCostType` is `Fixed`. Microsoft documents `Fixed` as a connection whose use is unrestricted only up to a specific limit:

   https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.networking.connectivity.networkcosttype

3. Set `network.meteredConnection` to `auto` in VS Code and restart VS Code.
4. Observe that the Metered Connection status bar indicator does not appear.
5. Open **Help > Toggle Developer Tools** and evaluate:

   ```js
   ({
     saveData: navigator.connection?.saveData,
     metered: navigator.connection?.metered,
     effectiveType: navigator.connection?.effectiveType
   })
   ```

   The result on the same connection is:

   ```js
   { saveData: false, metered: undefined, effectiveType: '3g' }
   ```

## Expected Behavior

With `network.meteredConnection` set to `auto`, VS Code should recognize a connection that Windows reports as `NetworkCostType.Fixed`, show the Metered Connection indicator, and postpone automatic update downloads and other protected background operations.

## Actual Behavior

VS Code treats the connection as non-metered. No Metered Connection indicator is shown, and automatic VS Code update downloads are allowed.

This is not only a UI discrepancy. In a previous normal VS Code session, I did not invoke an update action. The log shows checks recurring hourly, followed by a download at the next scheduled check:

```text
2026-08-07 13:27:15.508 [info] update#setState checking for updates
2026-08-07 13:27:21.486 [info] update#setState idle
2026-08-07 14:27:15.511 [info] update#setState checking for updates
2026-08-07 14:27:17.875 [info] update#setState downloading
...
2026-08-07 14:28:52.102 [info] update#setState downloaded
```

Another automatic update download left a 236,665,552-byte installer in `%TEMP%\vscode-stable-user-x64`. None of the available `main.log` files contains `skipping download because connection is metered`.

## Additional Diagnostics

The current implementation of `getIsBrowserConnectionMetered()` relies on `navigator.connection`. It returns `true` only when `saveData` or `metered` is truthy, or when `effectiveType` is `2g` or `slow-2g`:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960/src/vs/platform/meteredConnection/common/meteredConnection.ts#L58-L69

Chromium/Electron does not expose the Windows `NetworkCostType.Fixed` state through those values on this system, so VS Code's `auto` mode resolves to non-metered even though Windows explicitly reports the active connection as metered.

The closed test plan already notes that `navigator.connection` automatic detection "does not work well (or at all) currently," and one Windows test also reported that an update downloaded automatically:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/297205

I could not find an open issue specifically tracking broken Windows OS metered-state detection in `auto` mode. Related implementation issue and PR:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/103451
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/288919

The immediate cause might be upstream in Electron/Chromium, but the result is that VS Code's Windows `auto` mode does not honor the OS metered state. If this must be fixed upstream, it would still be useful to track the limitation here because it affects the behavior promised by this VS Code setting.

title: chat: index only content Find can reveal
body:
Follow-up to #330340. Fixes Find reporting matches it cannot navigate to.

## Symptoms

Searching a common word in a long transcript showed:

- a match count that **fell as rows rendered** — one session went `9999 → 4013 → 3793`, another `5949 → 705 → 240 → 123`
- **Next moving the counter without moving the view**
- Find jumping back to the first result while navigating

## Cause

The index reused `getChatResponsePlaintextParts`, the **accessible view's** extraction. That function describes a response to a screen reader rather than mirroring what is drawn, so it:

- synthesizes text with no on-screen equivalent — `Input:`, `Files:`, `Errored`, MCP authentication prompts
- includes tool result payloads, which live in a body that only exists once expanded

Matches in that text were counted, but the painter had nothing to highlight.

The count instability had a sharper cause: **`isAttachedToThinking` is assigned by the renderer** while drawing a row. A row that had not yet rendered looked un-grouped, so its tools were indexed; once drawn, they were excluded and those matches vanished. Navigating toward one meant targeting a match that ceased to exist.

## Changes

**New `chatFindContent.ts`** — a Find-specific extraction covering markdown, inline reference labels, elicitations and error details.

Reasoning and tool invocations are deliberately **not** indexed. Where a tool renders is decided during rendering, and reasoning bodies are built on expansion; indexing either makes the count depend on how far the transcript has drawn. This is the "start small" position — broadening it needs a typed expansion API on `ChatCollapsibleContentPart`, tracked separately.

**Repaint skips unrendered rows.** One memoized row lookup before scanning parts. In a captured trace, 51,298 of 51,363 locate attempts were for rows that were not on screen.

**Navigation advances past unlocatable matches** (bounded at 50), so Next never appears to do nothing if a prediction is still wrong.

## Tradeoff

Text inside a tool pill — including a terminal command header — is no longer searchable. Those matches were real and highlighted correctly, but keeping them requires reading render-time state, which is what produced the phantom results.

## Testing

- 47 targeted tests pass, including new cases for the extraction rule and a regression test that flips `isAttachedToThinking` after indexing and asserts the count is unchanged
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, ESLint clean
- Verified interactively against a long agent transcript: the count now holds steady and navigation moves

Diagnosed from console traces captured behind a temporary flag; the scaffolding is removed from this branch.

title: Subagent spawn in ACP/agent-host mode silently falls back to default model (claude-sonnet-5) when session uses BYOK, charging Copilot AI credits instead of BYOK provider
body:
### Describe the bug

When using GitHub Copilot CLI in ACP server mode (VS Code Agents window, agent-host
`chat.agentHost.enabled`), a session that selects a BYOK model (DeepSeek via VS Code's
customendpoint provider, exposed through a local proxy at `127.0.0.1:55845/v/customendpoint`)
works fine in the main session, but **every subagent spawn silently falls back to the
default Copilot model `claude-sonnet-5`**, which bills to Copilot AI credits instead of
the BYOK provider. The user believes all tokens go to their own DeepSeek endpoint, while
subagent traffic is actually charged to Copilot.

### Affected version


- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.60.0 (built-in, VS Code stable)
- VS Code Version: 1.132.0 (also reproduced on 1.134.0-insider)
- OS Version: macOS 15.7.7 (24G720)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window (agent-host mode, `chat.agentHost.enabled: true`), subagent spawn (general-purpose / explore / research)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): DeepSeek BYOK — `DeepSeek BYOK/deepseek-v4-pro` and `DeepSeek BYOK/deepseek-v4-flash` (customendpoint provider via VS Code local proxy `http://127.0.0.1:55845/v/customendpoint`)
- Logs: `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log` (GitHub Copilot CLI 0.0.421), e.g. 2026-08-12T01:48:11.593Z:



### Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open the VS Code Agents window (Copilot CLI in stdio ACP mode, `chat.agentHost.enabled: true`, `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled: true`).
2. In the session model picker, select a BYOK model (e.g. DeepSeek V4 Pro / Flash under "DeepSeek BYOK").
3. Ask the main agent to delegate work to a subagent (general-purpose, explore, research).
4. Observe the fallback warnings above; the subagent runs on `claude-sonnet-5` (Copilot default), not the selected BYOK model.

**Expected:** the subagent inherits the parent session's BYOK model, or the client fails loudly instead of silently falling back to a Copilot-billed model (users assume BYOK traffic costs nothing on Copilot, while subagent traffic is actually billed to Copilot AI credits).

**Actual:** silent fallback to `claude-sonnet-5` for every subagent spawn. Over the past week: 16× `Using default model: claude-sonnet-5` lines / 32 fallback warnings, all triggered when a subagent process starts — the BYOK custom provider is only visible to the main session, not to subagent processes.
